name: The Yale Review
pays: $250-$1,000 for prose depending on length; $150 for poems
notes: Open for nonfiction pitches AND completed drafts; criticism = review essays/critical essays, not straight reviews. No interview pitches. Fiction and poetry closed (2026). Response: assume pass after 4 weeks.

name: The Rumpus (Criticism)
pays: $500 reviews & essays; $200 interviews
word_count: Pitch 500 words or less; completed essays 1,200-5,000
notes: Pitches or finished essays via Submittable. Pay NOT stated on the Submittable page; figure is from NBCC sheet (updated 7/16/26). Cultural criticism incl. books, theatre, music, art; no tear-downs without substance.

name: The Drift
pays: $2,000 for essays; $25 for 'Mentions' (1-4 sentence reviews)
notes: Pitches only for nonfiction (2-4 paragraphs, one at a time); no draft essays. Very rarely publishes straight single-book reviews. Commissions ~5-6 months before publication (Pitching-the-Drift PDF). Pay also on the Drift 'About' page.

name: Literary Hub
pays: $200 (NBCC sheet; not stated on pitch page)
notes: Wants 'rigorous criticism for a general audience'; 2-3 paragraph pitch or finished essay. Not taking interview pitches; no fiction/poetry; no generative-AI pieces. Pay/word count from NBCC sheet (updated 6/13/23) - re-verify.

name: Chicago Review of Books
pays: $25 reviews and interviews; $75 features
notes: Pitch reviews/interviews ~2 months before book pub date. Prefers small press, BIPOC, LGBTQ+, Midwestern, translated titles. Cannot reply to every pitch.

name: Full Stop
pays: Pays for feature-length essays only (special-issue calls in 2025 listed $150-$200 essays, $100 reviews, $50 interviews)
notes: Year-round pitches/submissions, no fee. No fiction, poetry, or creative nonfiction. Rates for reviews appear only in themed 'Call for Pitches' posts (e.g. https://www.full-stop.net/2025/03/25/blog/the-editors/call-for-pitches-3/); those are dated 2025. Special-call terms seen via search excerpt; the open/year-round and essays-only-pay lines were confirmed on the fetched masthead page.

name: Words Without Borders
pays: $175 book reviews; $175 interviews; nonfiction $150/1,000 words capped at $350
word_count: Not stated for reviews (general avg. 2,000-2,500; ~4,000 max per older call)
notes: General submissions CLOSED since 2026-08-10 (no reopening date given). Book-review pitches still accepted for books publishing 4+ months out.

name: Cleveland Review of Books
pays: $150 online; $400 print (print interviews $200)
notes: Pitches or submissions of critical writing to pitches@ (2-5 paragraph pitch); everything considered for both online and print; aims to respond within 6 weeks. Rates raised from $100 online / $200 print (seen 2026-10-23) to $150 / $400 (seen 2026-10-26). Regional (Cleveland/Ohio/Rust Belt/Midwest) focus preferred but not required. Note: a different domain (clereviewofbooksonline.com) shows older terms - ignore.

name: The Markaz Review
pays: Honorarium paid within 30 days of publication (amount not stated on page); NBCC sheet lists $120
notes: Non-profit. Pitch an editor with a strong point of view; prefers comparative review essays; discourages reviewing friends. Dollar figure from NBCC (1/20/22) - stale.

name: Oxford American
pays: $300 flat fee for 'Dispatches'; $100 honorarium for a second project series (see page)
notes: Page seen lists specific pitch series (Dispatches), not a general book-review desk. No generative AI. Email pitch is free.

name: Polyester
pays: £65 flat rate (NBCC sheet; not stated on page)
notes: 'Pitches ... are always open.' Arts/culture deep dives, internet culture. Pays contributors (funded by members) per page; amount from NBCC (7/17/24). No AI use.

name: Reactor (formerly Tor.com)
pays: unpublished (page says they pay for original content, rates sent on acceptance); NBCC sheet lists $150 per piece
notes: Does not encourage spec articles; reviews need advance pitches (strict deadlines). SF/F/pop culture focus.

name: Slate
pays: Rates start at $350, increase with reporting/scope (NBCC sheet; not on pitch page)
notes: Pitch page lists editors by section; NBCC notes 'arguments and literary essays, not reviews'. Pay/word count from NBCC (undated) - re-verify.

name: The Toronto Review of Books
pays: $150 for published prose; $125 for interviews
notes: Reviews: pitch only (200-300 word pitch), no completed drafts. Poetry pitches not accepted. Fiction: full drafts only.

name: EVENT
pays: $40/page for poetry and book reviews; $35/page prose; max $500
notes: Reviews: read sample reviews, then contact the Reviews Editor before writing or submitting (completed reviews not accepted cold). Pay $40/page for reviews, paid on publication, plus 2 copies. Fiction reviews cover two books, poetry reviews three. Fiction/poetry windows closed until Dec 1; 2026 Non-Fiction Contest closed Oct 15.

name: Hyperallergic
pays: unpublished (third-party sites report $250-$500; not confirmed by outlet)
notes: Art/culture; pitches to the pitch inbox; no reply guaranteed - after 10 business days free to pitch elsewhere. No friend/self coverage.

name: The Nation
pays: $950-$1,250 print (NBCC sheet; not stated on page)
notes: Pitches only. Books & the Arts welcomes short pitches (a couple of sentences + clips). Decision within 2 weeks if pursued. Pay is NBCC (1/20/22) - stale.

name: Booklist
pays: $15 per published review ($5 for rejected titles) + print subscription
notes: Recruiting reviewers via a new-reviewer application (library readers' advisory/selection experience highly desired; library degree not required). $15 per published review, $5 reject fee, plus print subscription with online access; average reviewer writes 2-3 reviews/month; recommendation-only journal; no AI. Page fetched in full 2026-11-02 (previously seen only via search excerpt).

name: Kirkus Reviews (Kirkus Indie)
pays: unpublished (NBCC sheet lists $50 for trade sections)
word_count: About 350 words, due 2 weeks after assignment
notes: Careers page: looking for experienced reviewers of English/Spanish titles for Kirkus Indie. Application = resume + samples (contact by email per page).

name: The Baffler
pays: 'All contributions ... are paid' (amount not on page); NBCC sheet lists $400+
notes: Nonfiction as 2-paragraph pitch, no complete manuscripts. Rate from NBCC (2/2/23).

name: Jewish Currents
pays: $400 minimum for analysis and review pieces; in-depth web features $1,000+; print features $1/word (freelancer agreement)
notes: Wants reviews of literature, art and culture that make an argument; no capsule reviews and nothing on books/films/exhibits older than six months. Pitch answers why, why now, why you. Paid 25% on draft, 75% on completion (rates: jewishcurrents.org/jewish-currents-freelancer-agreement). Fiction closed; poetry June only.

name: Public Books
pays: unpublished
notes: Email pitch of 500 words or fewer with 'PITCH' in the subject; reviews within 6 months of the work's publication; one pitch at a time; response in 2-4 weeks. Interview pitches need an edited transcript (up to 5,000 words). No AI-generated or AI-revised writing at any stage.

name: In These Times
pays: Minimums per NWU agreement: $0.25-$0.50/word in print; $375 for online features/opinion/editorial; $150 for Q&A interviews; $250 for roundtables; $100 under 250 words
notes: NWU freelance agreement on inthesetimes.com guarantees written contract, payment within 30 days of publication (or signed contract), kill fee within 120 days, 50% of commercial reprint fees, and bans licensing freelancer work for LLM/generative AI training without 90-day prior written consent.

name: Los Angeles Review of Books
notes: Page: 'LARB welcomes pitches for our online publication on an open basis' (email a section editor or use the form). Pay not stated on page; NBCC figure is old.

name: Guernica
pays: $100 honorarium upon publication for Global Spotlights Book Reviews (1,200-2,500 words) and Spotlights Fiction/Nonfiction; NBCC sheet lists $150 for general essays
word_count: Global Spotlights book reviews 1,200-2,500 words; general nonfiction/critical essays 2,500+ words (typically 4,000-5,000)
notes: Completed manuscripts only via Submittable (no pitches). General Nonfiction (2,500+ words) welcomes longform critical essays engaging several texts/ideas (no single-book reviews). Global Spotlights: Book Reviews ($100 honorarium, 1,200-2,500 words) covers books published outside the West (US, UK, Canada, Western Europe, Australia, NZ) or by Indigenous writers within those regions. Simultaneous submissions accepted; 90-day exclusive rights.

name: Harvard Review
pays: Does not pay (NBCC sheet, 5/5/26)
notes: FAQ on site: no unsolicited book reviews; email reviews@ address (public) with desired books + clips. FAQ entry is dated 2018 - re-verify.

name: AGNI
pays: $30 per printed page for prose (reviews earn the same rate as prose), up to $300, plus a one-year subscription; no submission fee for reviews or pitches
notes: Reading periods Sep 1-Dec 15 and Jan 15-May 31 (11:59pm ET); currently open until Dec 15. No submission fee for review or pitch submissions ($3 online fee applies only to general fiction/poetry/essay submissions). Review essays 1,500-3,000 words (single- or multi-book inquiry-driven essays, esp. small/university press & translations; no round-ups/lists). Conflict-of-interest disclosure required; simultaneous submissions/pitches allowed with immediate notice; all reviews appear online.

name: The Common
pays: $250 for ~800-word reviews; $450 for ~1,500-word reviews
notes: Expanded book-review section: books with a strong sense of place from small independent presses, released within the last three months; no self-published books; honest criticism welcome. Pitch a review (or propose a book) via the form on the page. General reading periods Mar 1-Jun 1 and Sep 1-Dec 1.

name: Poets & Writers Magazine
pays: Paid when scheduled for production (exact rate not stated on guidelines page; buys exclusive worldwide periodical/syndication rights and 50/50 reprint rights)
notes: Queries/on-spec articles about writing life and the business; NO book reviews, fiction or poetry. Not a review market.

name: Electric Literature
pays: $100 for cultural criticism & personal narrative essays; $75 for reading lists (if not promoting own book); $300 for Recommended Reading fiction; $100 for The Commuter
word_count: Cultural criticism essays ≤3,500 words (email pitch); reading lists 7-10 books; personal narrative 2,000-6,500 words
notes: Cultural criticism pitches accepted year-round by email (pitches@electricliterature.com, subject "ESSAY PITCH: [title]", currently booking 2027 schedule); uses books/art/media as a lens rather than straight book reviews. Reading list pitches ("Reading List Pitch: [Topic]") pay $75. Generative AI strictly prohibited for creation or revision in any category.

name: Big Other
pays: No pay ("We are not a paying venue")
notes: Reviews of books, film, music, and art up to 6,000 words via dedicated Submittable channel (no submission fee for reviews/interviews; most other categories charge a fee). Simultaneous submissions encouraged with immediate withdrawal notice; 90-day exclusive rights.

name: New Letters
pays: $25 typical for book reviews; not guaranteed (paid as resources allow)
notes: Book reviews via Submittable year-round; small submission fee (waived for subscribers). Prefers good books not getting national attention; disclose conflicts; would rather skip a book than run a substantially negative review.

name: Compulsive Reader
pays: No monetary compensation (author bio with unlimited links and review copies provided)
notes: Reviews of books and music; must be analytical (no plot summary or blurbs); unpaid, author bio with links.

name: Boston Review
pays: About $500 for web pieces for writers whose main income is writing; modest honorarium for others
notes: Long-form argumentative essays and book reviews via Submittable (pitch or draft). Not in the NBCC sheet.

name: Asymptote
pays: Unpaid for blog reviews ('finances do not permit us to pay contributors'); occasional paid special calls (e.g. $100/article Czech showcase, Fall 2026)
notes: Blog: essays, reviews, dispatches, interviews on translated literature (1,500-2,500; reviews within 3 months of publication; pitches by email). Seeking regular columnists for "What's New in Translation", now shortform ~400-word reviews, 3-4 titles per quarter (apply with bio, cover letter, portfolio). Criticism section (2,000-5,000, via Submittable, USD10 fee) relaunching with a new approach in 2027. General policy: "Our finances do not permit us to pay contributors"; special features occasionally pay (Czech showcase $100/article, closed Oct 1, 2026).

name: The Brooklyn Rail
pays: $75 (NBCC sheet, 3/17/23)
notes: Pitch the relevant section editor (section@ addresses); editors cannot answer every email. Fiction not open; unsolicited poetry only in June and December (from 2026). Pay is old NBCC figure.

name: Another Chicago Magazine
pays: None (NBCC sheet, 4/28/26)
notes: Reviews and review-queries via Submittable/Tally; small/indie/university-press fiction & nonfiction (forthcoming or released this calendar year); no children's/YA. Book Reviews deadline Dec 1 (page 2026-11-09). Pay: none listed on the page (NBCC sheet 4/28/26: none).

name: Washington Independent Review of Books
pays: $100 per accepted submission for pitched book/reading/writing essays (no kill fee); $25 for reviews (NBCC sheet, 1/20/22)
notes: Page: pitches accepted for book-related pieces but REVIEWS ARE ASSIGNED IN-HOUSE (reach out with clips).

name: Foreword Reviews
pays: $55 per review
notes: Rolling freelance-reviewer hiring; one month per assignment; keep the book. Application by email to the managing editor (public on page).

name: Los Angeles Times
notes: No current public freelance book-review pitch guidelines found. Historical: freelance reviewers were cut in 2011 (reported by PW/The Stranger). NBCC lists $400 (updated 3/6/24) - conflicting; treat as unconfirmed.

name: The Boston Globe
notes: No public book-review pitch page found. The Globe Ideas desk publishes a submission page (https://www.bostonglobe.com/2020/05/14/opinion/submit-globe-ideas/): completed pieces only, no pitches, for op-eds, essays, book excerpts. Reviews: unclear.

name: NPR (Books)
notes: No freelance review intake found; NPR's own public-editor/FAQ pages describe books being booked by individual programs.

name: The Wall Street Journal
notes: No public freelance book-review pitch page found (only op-ed guidelines).

name: USA Today
notes: No public freelance pitch page for books found (Travel has a form).

name: Star Tribune (Minneapolis)
notes: Books editor Chris Hewitt's June 2025 column: staffers and several freelancers write reviews; reviewers sometimes ask to review books they're looking forward to. (Minnesota authors get extra coverage; that is about books covered, not reviewers.) No formal pitch page; pay is NBCC-sourced.

name: San Francisco Chronicle
notes: No public freelance book-review pitch page found; Chronicle's own article says books coverage prioritizes Bay Area angles.

name: The Christian Science Monitor
pays: $200 (NBCC sheet, 2/8/22; not stated on outlet page)
notes: Email query of a paragraph or two to the humanities editor; mainly literary fiction and nonfiction incl. history and memoir; mainstream and academic presses only, no self-published books; high volume, so not every pitch gets a reply.

name: The Atlanta Journal-Constitution
notes: No public freelance book-review pitch page found.

name: St. Louis Post-Dispatch
pays: $85 and up
notes: No outlet guideline page found; only third-party/old blog advice (physical galley ~4 weeks pre-pub; St. Louis angle). Not usable as a current guide.

name: Publishers Weekly
pays: $25 - $50 (NBCC sheet, 1/20/22; not stated on outlet page)
word_count: About 200 words (sample review requested); NBCC lists 220-260
notes: Trade reviews (~200 words) assigned by genre editors; prospective freelance reviewers email resume and ~200-word sample review to reviews_editors@publishersweekly.com. NBCC sheet lists $25 honorarium per review.

name: Library Journal
pays: No pay
notes: Recruiting reviewers via online application + two sample reviews in LJ style; all reviews are assigned, unsolicited reviews not accepted. Pay: page excerpt does not state; NBCC says no pay.

name: The New Republic
pays: $500-$2000 for print, $250-400 for web (NBCC sheet, 1/20/22; not stated on outlet page)
notes: Freelance pitches and unsolicited submissions by email to ONE editor (pitches sent to several editors get no reply); explain angle, timeliness and why you; hyperlink references. Rates are NBCC-sourced.

name: The New Yorker
pays: On web, 75c/word up to $1000
word_count: across print and web, anywhere from 1500 to 4500. Web pieces usually have a ceiling of 3k.
notes: No unsolicited nonfiction pitches or articles. Open freelance channels are fiction (reopened Nov 1, 2026 via Submittable), poetry, Shouts & Murmurs, cartoons. So 'closed' for criticism.

name: The New Criterion
notes: Only poetry submission guidance is public; no article/review pitch guidelines.

name: Reason
pays: Fees vary; paid on publication (outlet page). NBCC sheet (1/20/22): $500 for a full-length review
notes: Rarely accepts unsolicited manuscripts; prefers queries with background and clips; exclusive to Reason; assume no if no reply within a week. Most pieces run only on Reason.com (600-1,000 words). Libertarian perspective expected.

name: Vulture
pays: $300-$800 (NBCC sheet, 10/17/22; not stated on outlet page)
notes: Reviews of new releases go to staff and trusted freelance critics; to write criticism, pitch a focused angle on one aspect of a work or a group of related works (e.g. its 'Close Reads' format). No spec articles or junket Q&As; pitch the beat editor.

name: Paste Magazine
notes: Writer-guidelines page: main site no longer accepts unsolicited articles/pitches (works with a limited freelance team). Paste Food accepts pitches separately.

name: Chicago Reader
pays: From $75 (short pieces and capsule reviews, 200-300 words); $150 longer pieces or reviews; $200 features/columns (800-1,500 words); $250-$300 features (1,500-2,000 words)
notes: Mostly staff-written but runs freelance criticism. 2-3 paragraph email pitch to the section editor (books/visual arts, theater, film each have one); show serious expertise when pitching a review; film/theater capsules are assigned 3-4 weeks ahead. Paid within seven days of publication.

name: Lux Magazine
pays: $0.50 per word (NBCC sheet, 2/8/22; not stated on outlet page)
notes: 'Lux welcomes pitches': short email outlining the idea and why you should write it. Coverage runs from political reporting to reviews (e.g. of new novels). Third-party report: features ~$1/word.

name: LIBER: A Feminist Review
pays: $100 per book review; features $100-$300 (paid on publication)
notes: Pitch 3-4 months before publication with pub date, publisher, angle and case for significance; occasionally assigns already-published books. No reviews of books by friends/teachers/close colleagues; unlikely to cover self-published or hybrid-published books.

name: The Ex-Puritan (formerly The Puritan)
pays: CAD $100 per review ($200 essays, $100 interviews; rates as of Fall 2022 per its Submittable page)
notes: Reviews of CanLit books (esp. marginalized and debut authors, chapbooks) via Submittable year-round; a fully thought-out pitch is acceptable. Winter 2027 categories open until Dec 25; the free category has a monthly cap (a $3 fee category stays open). Decision within 4 months. Pays only by e-transfer, PayPal or Canadian cheque. The old domain puritan-magazine.com now shows unrelated content; the magazine is at ex-puritan.ca.

name: On the Seawall
pays: $100 (NBCC sheet, 1/20/22; not stated on outlet page)
notes: For commentary and reviews, contact them first and say what you have in mind; reviews across the arts and humanities from independent, university and corporate presses. No submission fee; no AI-generated work.

name: Necessary Fiction
pays: No pay
notes: Info page covers publishers/authors sending books for review (literary fiction, esp. translations), not recruiting freelance reviewers. NBCC says pitch with clips; unpaid.

name: Barrelhouse
pays: No pay ("we do not pay for book reviews at this time")
notes: Finished book reviews via Submittable (online only, unpaid). Strong preference for small-press, weird, hybrid titles published within ±6 months (up to 1 year); no self-published titles, no book essays, unlikely to cover major houses. Simultaneous submissions encouraged.

name: London Review of Books
pays: unpublished
notes: UK. Unsolicited submissions AND proposals welcome (reviews, reportage, memoir, Short Cuts/Diary, blog). No AI. Assume no if silent after 3 weeks. Pay not stated on page. (Page fetched.)

name: Times Literary Supplement (TLS)
pays: unpublished
notes: UK. Reviews are commissioned from a reviewer pool; no current public pitch page found (2019 TLS freelance feature is dated). Third-party advice: send CV + clips to join pool.

name: Literary Review (UK)
pays: unpublished
notes: UK. Contact page lists an editorial address for review/feature proposals (short outline first).

name: New Statesman
pays: unpublished
notes: UK. Pitch the relevant culture/books editor, one idea per email, no unsolicited drafts. Source is third-party (Press Gazette / Women in Journalism); no outlet guideline page found.

name: Prospect (UK)
pays: Paid (fee negotiated before acceptance; writing from think-tanks, politicians, academics, and charities generally unpaid)
notes: UK. Send concise pitch + bio + 1-2 clips to webdesk@prospect-magazine.co.uk; no unsolicited finished pieces; no simultaneous pitches (state deadline in email if needed). Aims to reply to commissioned pitches within 24 hours.

name: The Critic (UK)
pays: unpublished
notes: UK. No formal 'write for us' page; accepts pitches and unsolicited articles via its editorial address; rejects AI-assisted work (their own article says so).

name: Dublin Review of Books
pays: unpublished
notes: Ireland. Open to all contributors: email or use the contact form with a brief overview of what you'd like to write. Long-form essays and shorter pieces, usually tied to recent books; up to half Irish subjects, strong interest in Europe. About page (fetched 2026-10-19) states neither pay nor lengths; the 3,000-6,000 figure came from an earlier search excerpt.

name: The Johannesburg Review of Books
pays: Pays for published writing (amount not stated on the pages seen)
notes: South Africa. Content mostly solicited; wants longer critical reviews of trade-published books in Africa/Commonwealth from the last year; other pitches may get no reply.

name: Sydney Review of Books
pays: $1,500 flat for published longform articles (per excerpt of the Write for SRB page)
notes: Australia. Not accepting unsolicited pitches at the moment (Submittable has no open call). When open: bio ≤100 words, pitch ≤250, writing sample ≤800; up to three pitches. Watch for next call.

name: Australian Book Review
pays: Pays for everything it publishes, print or online (rates not stated on page)
notes: Australia. Currently welcomes pitches for commentary essays on political and cultural topics. New reviewers should read its 'Advice for New Reviewers'; ~80 of ~300 contributors a year are new. No generative AI.

name: Overland (Australia)
pays: $180 online articles/poems; $580 print fiction & essays (+ super and GST where applicable)
notes: Australia. Pitch through its submission system (~100-word proposal; separate subscriber and non-subscriber links) or send a completed online piece. Prefers expansive review essays connecting several texts over single-text reviews. Online focus currently includes Palestine; no personal essays online. $180 per online piece confirmed on the pitch page.

name: Meanjin (Australia)
pays: Pays all published work (print and online) on publication; rates not stated on page
notes: Australia; primarily publishes Australian writers. Current open call (December 2026 edition) is fiction & poetry only. Book reviews/criticism 1,500-3,000 (print); also "Australia in Three Books" (1,500-2,500) and "The Year In..." (1,500-3,500); short online pieces fortnightly. No pitches from publicists; no AI-prepared work.

name: Kill Your Darlings (Australia)
pays: Aug 2025 call: at least $700 for nonfiction; New Critics program paid $1,237 per 1,200-word review (per excerpts)
notes: Australia. Pitches open in periodic calls; New Critics program applications closed when checked. Figures are from 2025 calls - re-verify.

name: Literary Review of Canada
pays: unpublished
notes: Canada. Unsolicited review-topic and essay pitches on a rolling basis; rarely accepts completed work; no simultaneous submissions.

name: Brick (Canada)
pays: CAD $65-$720 depending on length, plus two copies and a one-year subscription
notes: Canada. Literary non-fiction (essays, reviews, interviews) - finished work via Submittable only. Windows: Oct 1-31 and Apr 1-30; the October 2026 window has closed; next window Apr 1-30, 2027. Free-submission cap often fills early. Response up to a year. (Page fetched.)

name: n+1
pays: unpublished
notes: US. New fiction, essays, criticism and translation by email (poetry to a separate address); no art, illustration or interview submissions; strong emphasis on work by and about living authors. Three print issues a year plus an online section; may not reply to everyone.

name: The Point Magazine
pays: Pays contributors for print and online pieces (amount not stated)
notes: US. Pitches or drafts via Submittable. Reviews 'can be about pretty much anything' but no straight book/film reviews: wants narrative plus a philosophical or critical argument. Criticism about fiction and poetry welcome. Disclose any generative-AI use.

name: Aeon
pays: Not publicly listed: freelance fee or honorarium disclosed before contracting (a 2025 university page reports £600)
notes: Currently closed for pitches (per excerpt of its pitch page). Pitch only, no drafts.

name: The Believer
pays: unpublished
notes: No open submissions or calls for pitches when checked.

name: Bookforum
pays: unpublished
notes: Contact page: pitches and galleys go to the editors' address; review copies ≥3 months pre-pub, PDF preferred.

name: The Atlantic (Books/Culture)
pays: unpublished
notes: Help-center page: pitch reported stories or commentary for the website by email to the matching desk; books and culture go to the Culture and Books desk (culture@theatlantic.com). The Atlantic replies only if interested. Pay not published.

name: The Guardian (Books)
pays: UK: £0.39408/word (£394.08 per 1,000 words), blog £109.05; US: $500 per 1,000 words ($0.50/word), blog/opinion $150; Australia: AUD $0.81/word, reviews AUD $348 (GNM Freelance Charter eff. 22 Oct 2026)
notes: Pitch the relevant section commissioning editor before writing; speculative submissions paid only if published. Commissioned pieces carry a 100% kill fee (or ≥50% if substantially below brief), paid within 30 business days of publication; writer retains copyright with 90-day exclusive syndication license to GNM.

name: Wasafiri
pays: £50 for book reviews; £150 for review essays, interviews, and fiction/life writing; £50 for poems
word_count: Single-title reviews 1,100-1,200; double-title reviews 1,400-1,500; review essays 2,400-2,500; critical academic articles 6,000-9,000; interviews 4,000-5,000
notes: UK. Book review pitches currently closed (Reviews Editor: Abhay Puri, wasafiri.reviews@qmul.ac.uk); interviews (4,000-5,000 words, £150) and peer-reviewed critical academic articles (6,000-9,000 words, 9-12 mo decision) open year-round via online portal. AI-generated content or machine translation prohibited and treated as plagiarism.

name: The Millions
pays: unpublished
notes: No current public pitch page found; only old interviews/guidance. In NBCC sheet with no data.

name: Ancillary Review of Books
pays: $50 for standard reviews (700-1,000 words); $75 for short essays/columns (1,500-2,000 words); $100 for longer essays/columns (2,500-3,000 words) (Year 7 honoraria, 7/1/2026-6/30/2027)
notes: Speculative fiction, cultural studies & translated lit reviews/essays. Monthly Calls for Reviews & Essays (latest: January 2027 titles); also open to series, re-reads, and ARB Guides. Honoraria disbursed first week of month after publication; no kill fee; CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 license. Categorically rejects generative AI at any stage of writing.

name: Still Point: Poetry & Culture
pays: No pay (unpaid, no fee)
notes: Poetry-book reviews only. Window for March issue: Nov 1-30, 2026; submit complete copyedited review by email. (Page fetched.)

name: Drafting the Past
pays: $200 per single-book review; more for review essays
word_count: Single-book reviews up to 1,000; review essays up to 1,500
notes: Nonfiction history books only (university presses welcome, not purely academic titles). Email pitch with 'BOOK REVIEW' in the subject at least three months before publication; newspaper/magazine style, not academic. Follow every instruction on the page (it includes a check phrase). No reply within two weeks = declined. No gen-AI.

name: Grain Magazine (Canada)
pays: CAD $50 per printed page, up to $250, plus two copies
notes: Canada. New call for pitches for short book reviews, interviews and craft essays, accepted on a rolling basis by email (outline of 250 words max; subject 'Pitch, Theme, Your Name'). Regular submissions Sep 15-Jun 15. No AI-assisted work.

name: The Threepenny Review
pays: $400 per article (critical articles included); $200 per Table Talk piece
word_count: Critical articles about 1,200-2,500; Table Talk up to 1,000
notes: US. Reads only Jan 1-Apr 14; non-reading period Apr 15-Dec 31 (closed now, reopens Jan 1, 2027). Online or mailed submissions, never email. Reviews must be essays broader than the book/show/exhibit they cover. Replies in two days to two weeks online.

name: WritersReview
pays: $125-$250 per review
notes: US / global. Rolling reviewer application on /write-for-us/; editors assign books in the reviewer's genre specialty across 12 genres (Literary Fiction, Sci-Fi, Biography, History, Poetry, Philosophy, etc.). Prioritizes reviewers with a published book or editing/acquisitions experience. Never charges authors or publishers for coverage ($0 fee). Contact: editorial@writersreview.com.

general_submission.scope: Book review consideration (publishers, publicists, agents, authors)
general_submission.fee: $0 (no fee for review consideration; no paid reviews)

review_submission.scope: Paid book reviewers (rolling application, assigned by genre)

name: Michigan Quarterly Review (MQR Online)
pays: $50 for all MQR Online contributions
notes: US. MQR Online publishes book reviews, essays, arts and culture features and author interviews; brief pitches or submissions year-round via the free "MQR Online Pitches and Submissions" Submittable form; the Online Editor invites selected pitches to submit a full piece. AI-generated work rarely accepted and must be disclosed.

name: Strange Horizons
pays: $60 per review (1,000+ words); $150 original essay; $75 column; $45 interviewer + $45 interviewee; $20 roundtable contributors
notes: SF & fantasy (books, film, TV), reviews published three times a week; usually works from the last 12-18 months. Pitch or send reviews on spec to reviews@ ("REVIEWS SUB: title"); essay/interview/roundtable queries to articles@ with [QUERY]. Response ~2 weeks (reviews), 4 weeks (articles). No GenAI. Essay/roundtable rates from its Nonfiction guidelines page.

name: Split Lip Magazine
pays: $100 per review or interview; $50 per micro review
notes: Reviews and interviews of literary collections released within the last nine months or forthcoming. Send a description of the review or the completed review via the query form (or email a Word doc). No reviews of friends/family; no resubmitting rejected work; keeps no list of books or stable of reviewers.

name: Reckoning
pays: $75 flat per fiction review; $37.50 flat per nonfiction review
notes: Critical reviews (strong thesis, quotes, sources/footnotes welcome) of fiction and nonfiction that center environmental justice; mostly books from the last year, independent presses and historically marginalized authors preferred. Pitches welcome but not required (300-word pitch + bio + 1-2 clips). One open submission at a time, via its Moksha portal only (no email).

name: Infrarrealista Review
pays: $100 per review; $100 per essay; $50 per interview
notes: Nonprofit publishing Tejanx voices; page says "We are currently open". Book reviews of small-press books, books by Texan writers, and out-of-print Texas books; also cultura essays (film, pop culture; pitches or completed essays; Texan writers prioritized). Submit through the site, not email. Some work appears in its "Letras Y Disparates" section of the Caldwell-Hays Examiner.
